title: Paraguay's President Removed From Office After Bank Collapse
summary:
Paraguay's president has been removed from office after a bank collapse left millions of people unable to reach their money. President Santiago Peña was impeached on Friday, just days after Ueno Bank, a digital bank, collapsed earlier in the week.

The bank's collapse left more than half of the country's population without access to their accounts. An estimated three million depositors still cannot reach their savings and pensions. The bank was seized by Paraguay's central bank, and people in the capital, Asunción, have taken to the streets in protest.

Lawmakers voted to remove Peña, including members of his own party. The Senate voted 44 to 0 in favor, with one lawmaker absent. The charges against him alleged conflicts of interest, interference with regulators, diverted pension funds, and a cover-up involving the central bank. Peña held shares until last year in the company that owned the bank, but he has denied any wrongdoing.

In a video posted online, Peña announced his resignation and said it was never his intention to betray the trust people had placed in him. Senate president Basilio Núñez said Peña was found guilty of failing in his duties. One senator called it the biggest corruption scandal in the country's democratic history. Peña is due to be questioned on Saturday over allegations of breach of trust, influence peddling, and misuse of funds. His lawyer called the allegations reckless and irresponsible.

Peña was arrested on Friday, minutes after the vote, and placed under house arrest. His deputy, Pedro Alliana, has been sworn in as interim president and will serve until 2028. Alliana promised that people affected by the financial collapse 'will be fully compensated.' Analysts say Peña is likely to face prosecution over the bank's collapse.
why_it_matters: When a bank fails, ordinary families can lose access to savings and pensions they depend on, so this case raises wider questions about who protects people's money and holds leaders accountable.

background_read: A bank holds people's savings and pensions, and a digital bank is one that people use online rather than by visiting a branch.
In Paraguay, Ueno Bank collapsed, leaving many people unable to reach their money, and the country's central bank, which oversees banks, seized it.

Lawmakers can remove a president from office through impeachment when they find that the president has failed in their duties, and that is what happened to President Santiago Peña after lawmakers linked him to the bank's troubles, though he has denied any wrongdoing.
